doc.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe. Utica, New York, November 6, 2010 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Woman in Jazz events and the Diva big band name
summary: Discussion of 'women in jazz' labeling, Billy Taylor's festival, and why Diva keeps its name.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Well it’s like referring to Marian McPartland as “one of the best of the women jazz musicians.”

Yeah. And still today. You know and certain clubs that shall remain nameless, but trying to get a gig there is, you might get a night on a “Woman in Jazz” week. You know and it’s kind of like wow, you still have those? Well I guess we do. And Billy Taylor has a wonderful Woman in Jazz Festival at the Kennedy Center. You know, but he’s doing it for the right reason. He’s doing it because he wants to highlight women leaders more. You know, so it’s not only women playing. And of course I’m friends with everybody in Diva and there’s a lot of wonderful musicians in Diva, where I started, in the Diva big band. My sister plays in Diva, and it’s a great band and I like everyone in the band. But there’s still some issues around it. We try not to take too much time about it.
Well do you think it would get to the point where the Diva big band could just be the something-else big band. I mean the title of the band calls attention to the fact that this is an all-women band.

Yeah. Well I guess it gets into the marketing thing. I mean I think it’s hard enough for a big band to get work. In fact my sister leaves today to go on a jazz cruise with Diva. Anyway, I think if you’ve been around for ten years and you get gigs with the name Diva and it’s working for you then why change it. I mean it’s hard enough with a name change to try to get gigs. I think it works for them. You know they are kind of a Diva-ish kind of band. You know what I mean? They really sock it to you. They’re a really fully charged band I think, with good players.
So the name does have some significance behind it. Because the word “Diva” is used a lot these days.
Yeah it’s overused and it’s usually in reference to a woman who thinks she’s all that or whatever. You know what I mean? But I think it’s fine for the band. And they sound good.
